question.problem:
Given that $6a≡6b\,(\text{mod}\,9),$ which of the following statements **must** be true?

- $2a≡2b\,(\text{mod}\,3)$
- $3a≡3b\,(\text{mod}\,6)$
- $a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,9)$
question.worked_solution:
The division property of modular arithmetic states that for $k\ne 0,$ we have

$$
ka≡kb\,(\text{mod}\,kn)\,⟺\,a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n).
$$

We're asked to consider the following statement:

$$
6a≡6b\,(\text{mod}\,9)
$$

Notice that $\text{gcd}(6,9)=3.$

Applying the division property, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}6a & ≡6b &  & (\text{mod}\,9) \\ 3\cdot 2\cdot a & ≡3\cdot 2\cdot b &  & (\text{mod}\,3\cdot 3) \\ \cancel{3}\cdot 2\cdot a & ≡\cancel{3}\cdot 2\cdot b &  & (\text{mod}\,\cancel{3}\cdot 3) \\ 2a & ≡2b &  & (\text{mod}\,3)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only".
